iconicAnchor.label: My Yia Vang's Hmong Story Cloth
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The documented work clearly joins sequential reading, embroidered figures, landscape, layered borders, refugee history, maker biography, and sale within diaspora life.

sources.title: My Yia Vang's Hmong Story Cloth
supports: Hmong pictorial embroidery can carry sequential accounts of village life, displacement, migration, and refugee camps through figures, scenery, and bordered cloth.

sources.title: Hmong Story Cloths: Preserving Historical and Cultural Treasures
supports: Hmong story cloths visually document history and culture through outlined images, multicolored satin stitch, intricate details, and pieced borders.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches sequential stitched scenes, continuous cloth field, embroidered figures, applique borders, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/narrative-textile/reference-01.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.

culturalContext.note: Name the precise community, maker, place, and historical circumstances. Hmong paj ntaub, arpilleras, Bayeux-related works, and other narrative textiles have different origins and uses. Do not combine their motifs or treat migration, war, displacement, sacred history, or personal testimony as freely available decoration; foreground maker voice and context.
